Section_name: Short title, application and commencement
Description: (1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. (2) It applies to all judicial proceedings in or before any Court, including Courts-martial, but not to affidavits presented to any Court or officer, nor to proceedings before an arbitrator. (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

Section_name: Definitions
Description: (1) In this Adhiniyam, unless the context otherwise requires,— (a) 'Court' includes all Judges and Magistrates, and all persons, except arbitrators, legally authorised to take evidence; (b) 'conclusive proof' means when one fact is declared by this Adhiniyam to be conclusive proof of another, the Court shall, on proof of the one fact, regard the other as proved, and shall not allow evidence to be given for the purpose of disproving it; (c) 'disproved' in relation to a fact, means when, after considering the matters before it, the Court either believes that it does not exist, or considers its non-existence so probable that a prudent man ought, under the circumstances of the particular case, to act upon the supposition that it does not exist; (d) 'document' means any matter expressed or described or otherwise recorded upon any substance by means of letters, figures or marks or any other means or by more than one of those means, intended to be used, or which may be used, for the purpose of recording that matter and includes electronic and digital records; (e) 'evidence' means and includes— (i) all statements including statements given electronically which the Court permits or requires to be made before it by witnesses in relation to matters of fact under inquiry (oral evidence); (ii) all documents including electronic or digital records produced for the inspection of the Court (documentary evidence); (f) 'fact' means and includes— (i) any thing, state of things, or relation of things, capable of being perceived by the senses; (ii) any mental condition of which any person is conscious; (g) 'facts in issue' means and includes any fact from which, either by itself or in connection with other facts, the existence, non-existence, nature or extent of any right, liability or disability, asserted or denied in any suit or proceeding, necessarily follows; (h) 'may presume' whenever provided that the Court may presume a fact, it may either regard such fact as proved, unless and until it is disproved or may call for proof of it; (i) 'not proved'—A fact is said to be not proved when it is neither proved nor disproved; (j) 'proved'—A fact is said to be proved when, after considering the matters before it, the Court either believes it to exist, or considers its existence so probable that a prudent man ought, under the circumstances of the particular case, to act upon the supposition that it exists; (k) 'relevant'—A fact is said to be relevant to another when it is connected with the other in any of the ways referred to in the provisions of this Adhiniyam relating to the relevancy of facts; (l) 'shall presume'—Whenever directed that the Court shall presume a fact, it shall regard such fact as proved, unless and until it is disproved. (2) Words and expressions used herein and not defined but defined in the Information Technology Act, 2000, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 shall have the same meanings as assigned to them in the said Act and Sanhitas.

Section_name: Evidence may be given of facts in issue and relevant facts
Description: Evidence may be given in any suit or proceeding of the existence or non-existence of every fact in issue and of such other facts as are hereinafter declared to be relevant, and of no others. Explanation.—This section shall not enable any person to give evidence of a fact which he is disentitled to prove by any provision of the law for the time being in force relating to civil procedure.

Section_name: Relevancy of facts forming part of same transaction
Description: Facts which, though not in issue, are so connected with a fact in issue or a relevant fact as to form part of the same transaction, are relevant, whether they occurred at the same time and place or at different times and places.

Section_name: Facts which are occasion, cause or effect of facts in issue or relevant facts
Description: Facts which are the occasion, cause or effect, immediate or otherwise, of relevant facts, or facts in issue, or which constitute the state of things under which they happened, or which afforded an opportunity for their occurrence or transaction, are relevant.

Section_name: Motive, preparation and previous or subsequent conduct
Description: (1) Any fact is relevant which shows or constitutes a motive or preparation for any fact in issue or relevant fact. (2) The conduct of any party, or of any agent to any party, to any suit or proceeding, in reference to such suit or proceeding, or in reference to any fact in issue therein or relevant thereto, and the conduct of any person, an offence against whom is the subject of any proceeding, is relevant, if such conduct influences or is influenced by any fact in issue or relevant fact, and whether it was previous or subsequent thereto. Explanation 1.—The word 'conduct' in this section does not include statements, unless those statements accompany and explain acts other than statements. Explanation 2.—When the conduct of any person is relevant, any statement made to him or in his presence and hearing, which affects such conduct, is relevant.

Section_name: Facts necessary to explain or introduce fact in issue or relevant facts
Description: Facts necessary to explain or introduce a fact in issue or relevant fact, or which support or rebut an inference suggested by a fact in issue or a relevant fact, or which establish the identity of anything, or person whose identity, is relevant, or fix the time or place at which any fact in issue or relevant fact happened, or which show the relation of parties by whom any such fact was transacted, are relevant in so far as they are necessary for that purpose.

Section_name: Things said or done by conspirator in reference to common design
Description: Where there is reasonable ground to believe that two or more persons have conspired together to commit an offence or an actionable wrong, anything said, done or written by any one of such persons in reference to their common intention, after the time when such intention was first entertained by any one of them, is a relevant fact as against each of the persons believed to be so conspiring, as well for the purpose of proving the existence of the conspiracy as for the purpose of showing that any such person was a party to it.

Section_name: When facts not otherwise relevant become relevant
Description: Facts not otherwise relevant are relevant— (1) if they are inconsistent with any fact in issue or relevant fact; (2) if by themselves or in connection with other facts they make the existence or non-existence of any fact in issue or relevant fact highly probable or improbable.

Section_name: Facts tending to enable Court to determine amount are relevant in suits for damages
Description: In suits in which damages are claimed, any fact which will enable the Court to determine the amount of damages which ought to be awarded, is relevant.

Section_name: Facts relevant when right or custom is in question
Description: Where the question is as to the existence of any right or custom, the following facts are relevant— (a) any transaction by which the right or custom in question was created, claimed, modified, recognised, asserted or denied, or which was inconsistent with its existence; (b) particular instances in which the right or custom was claimed, recognised or exercised, or in which its exercise was disputed, asserted or departed from.

Section_name: Facts showing existence of state of mind, or of body or bodily feeling
Description: Facts showing the existence of any state of mind, such as intention, knowledge, good faith, negligence, rashness, ill-will or goodwill towards any particular person, or showing the existence of any state of body or bodily feeling, are relevant, when the existence of any such state of mind or body or bodily feeling is in issue or relevant. Explanation 1.—A fact relevant as showing the existence of a relevant state of mind must show that the state of mind exists, not generally, but in reference to the particular matter in question. Explanation 2.—Where the previous commission by the accused of an offence is relevant, the previous conviction of such person shall also be a relevant fact.

Section_name: Facts bearing on question whether act was accidental or intentional
Description: When there is a question whether an act was accidental or intentional, or done with a particular knowledge or intention, the fact that such act formed part of a series of similar occurrences, in each of which the person doing the act was concerned, is relevant.

Section_name: Existence of course of business when relevant
Description: When there is a question whether a particular act was done, the existence of any course of business, according to which it naturally would have been done, is a relevant fact.

Section_name: Admission defined
Description: An admission is a statement, oral or documentary or contained in electronic form, which suggests any inference as to any fact in issue or relevant fact, and which is made by any of the persons, and under the circumstances, hereinafter mentioned.

Section_name: Admission by party to proceeding or his agent
Description: (1) Statements made by a party to the proceeding, or by an agent to any such party, whom the Court regards as expressly or impliedly authorised by him to make them, are admissions. (2) Statements made by— (i) parties suing or sued in representative character (while holding that character); or (ii) persons having proprietary or pecuniary interest, or persons from whom interest is derived, during continuance of interest, are admissions.

Section_name: Admissions by persons whose position must be proved as against party to suit
Description: Statements made by persons whose position or liability, it is necessary to prove as against any party to the suit, are admissions, if such statements would be relevant as against such persons in relation to such position or liability in a suit brought by or against them, and if they are made whilst the person making them occupies such position or is subject to such liability.

Section_name: Admissions by persons expressly referred to by party to suit
Description: Statements made by persons to whom a party to the suit has expressly referred for information in reference to a matter in dispute are admissions.

Section_name: Proof of admissions against persons making them, and by or on their behalf
Description: Admissions are relevant and may be proved as against the person who makes them, or his representative in interest; but they cannot be proved by or on behalf of the person who makes them or by his representative in interest, except in specified cases (e.g. dying declaration equivalent under Sec 26, state of mind/body accompanied by conduct, or relevant otherwise than as admission).

Section_name: When oral admissions as to contents of documents are relevant
Description: Oral admissions as to the contents of a document are not relevant, unless and until the party proposing to prove them shows that he is entitled to give secondary evidence of the contents of such document, or unless the genuineness of a document produced is in question.

Section_name: Admissions in civil cases when relevant
Description: In civil cases no admission is relevant, if it is made either upon an express condition that evidence of it is not to be given, or under circumstances from which the Court can infer that the parties agreed together that evidence of it should not be given.

Section_name: Confession caused by inducement, threat, coercion or promise, when irrelevant in criminal proceeding
Description: A confession made by an accused person is irrelevant in a criminal proceeding, if the making of the confession appears to the Court to have been caused by any inducement, threat, coercion or promise having reference to the charge against the accused person, proceeding from a person in authority. Provided that if made after impression fully removed, it is relevant. Provided further that confession otherwise relevant does not become irrelevant merely because made under promise of secrecy, deception, drunkenness, or unwarned.

Section_name: Confession to police officer
Description: (1) No confession made to a police officer shall be proved as against a person accused of any offence. (2) No confession made by any person while in custody of a police officer, unless in immediate presence of a Magistrate, shall be proved against him. Provided that when any fact is deposed to as discovered in consequence of information received from an accused in custody, so much of such information as relates distinctly to the fact discovered may be proved.

Section_name: Consideration of proved confession affecting person making it and others jointly under trial for same offence
Description: When more persons than one are being tried jointly for the same offence, and a confession made by one of such persons affecting himself and some other of such persons is proved, the Court may take into consideration such confession as against such other person as well as against the person who makes such confession.

Section_name: Admissions not conclusive proof, but may estop
Description: Admissions are not conclusive proof of the matters admitted but they may operate as estoppels under the provisions hereinafter contained.

Section_name: Cases in which statement of relevant fact by person who is dead or cannot be found, etc., is relevant
Description: Statements, written or verbal, of relevant facts made by a person who is dead, or who cannot be found, or who has become incapable of giving evidence, or whose attendance cannot be procured without unreasonable delay/expense, are relevant facts in cases of: (a) Dying declaration (cause of death); (b) Ordinary course of business / account books / professional duty; (c) Against pecuniary or proprietary interest; (d) Opinion as to public right or custom; (e) Existence of relationship by blood, marriage or adoption; (f) Family pedigree, will, deed, tombstone, portrait; (g) Documents relating to transactions under Sec 11(a); (h) Expressed feelings of number of persons.

Section_name: Relevancy of Certain evidence for proving, in subsequent proceeding, truth of facts therein stated
Description: Evidence given by a witness in a judicial proceeding, or before any person authorised by law, is relevant for proving in a subsequent judicial proceeding, or later stage of same proceeding, truth of facts stated, when witness is dead, cannot be found, incapable, kept out by adverse party, or presence delayed/expensive: Provided proceeding was between same parties, adverse party had right/opportunity to cross-examine, and questions in issue substantially same.

Section_name: Entries in books of account when relevant
Description: Entries in the books of account, including those maintained in an electronic form, regularly kept in the course of business are relevant whenever they refer to a matter into which the Court has to inquire, but such statements shall not alone be sufficient evidence to charge any person with liability.

Section_name: Relevancy of entry in public record or an electronic record made in performance of duty
Description: An entry in any public or other official book, register or record or an electronic record, stating a fact in issue or relevant fact, and made by a public servant in the discharge of his official duty, or by any other person in performance of a duty specially enjoined by law, is itself a relevant fact.

Section_name: Relevancy of statements in maps, charts and plans
Description: Statements of facts in issue or relevant facts, made in published maps or charts generally offered for public sale, or in maps or plans made under the authority of Central or State Government, are relevant facts.

Section_name: Relevancy of statement as to fact of public nature contained in certain Acts or notifications
Description: When the Court has to form an opinion as to existence of any fact of a public nature, any statement of it in a recital contained in any Central or State Act or Government notification in Official Gazette or printed/electronic paper, is a relevant fact.

Section_name: Relevancy of statements as to any law contained in law books including electronic or digital form
Description: When the Court has to form an opinion as to law of any country, any statement contained in a book printed/published under authority of Government of such country, and reports of rulings of Courts of such country, is relevant.

Section_name: What evidence to be given when statement forms part of a conversation, document, electronic record, book or series of letters or papers
Description: When any statement forms part of a longer statement, conversation, isolated document, electronic record, or book/letters, evidence shall be given of so much and no more as the Court considers necessary to full understanding of nature and effect of statement and circumstances.

Section_name: Previous judgments relevant to bar a second suit or trial
Description: The existence of any judgment, order or decree which by law prevents any Court from taking cognizance of a suit or holding a trial, is a relevant fact when the question is whether such Court ought to take cognizance or hold trial.

Section_name: Relevancy of certain judgments in probate, etc., jurisdiction
Description: (1) A final judgment, order or decree of a competent Court or Tribunal, in exercise of probate, matrimonial, admiralty or insolvency jurisdiction, conferring/taking away legal character or declaring title to specific thing absolutely, is relevant. (2) Such judgment, order or decree is conclusive proof of such legal character or title.

Section_name: Relevancy and effect of judgments, orders or decrees, other than those mentioned in Section 35
Description: Judgments, orders or decrees other than those mentioned in Section 35 are relevant if they relate to matters of a public nature relevant to the enquiry; but such judgments, orders or decrees are not conclusive proof of that which they state.

Section_name: Judgments, etc., other than those mentioned in Sections 34, 35 and 36 when relevant
Description: Judgments or orders or decrees, other than those mentioned in Sections 34, 35 and 36, are irrelevant, unless the existence of such judgment, order or decree is a fact in issue, or is relevant under some other provision of this Adhiniyam.

Section_name: Fraud or collusion in obtaining judgment, or incompetency of Court, may be proved
Description: Any party to a suit or proceeding may show that any judgment, order or decree relevant under Section 34, 35 or 36 was delivered by a Court not competent to deliver it, or was obtained by fraud or collusion.

Section_name: Opinions of experts
Description: (1) When Court has to form opinion upon foreign law, science, art, identity of handwriting or finger impressions, or any other field, opinions of persons specially skilled (experts) are relevant. (2) When Court has to form opinion on information transmitted/stored in computer resource/electronic form, opinion of Examiner of Electronic Evidence (Sec 79A IT Act) is a relevant fact.

Section_name: Facts bearing upon opinions of experts
Description: Facts, not otherwise relevant, are relevant if they support or are inconsistent with the opinions of experts, when such opinions are relevant.

Section_name: Opinion as to handwriting and signature, when relevant
Description: (1) Opinion of any person acquainted with handwriting of person by whom document was written/signed is a relevant fact. (2) Opinion of Certifying Authority issuing Electronic Signature Certificate is relevant regarding electronic signature.

Section_name: Opinion as to existence of general custom or right, when relevant
Description: When Court has to form opinion as to existence of general custom or right, opinions of persons likely to know of its existence if it existed, are relevant.

Section_name: Opinion as to usages, tenets, etc., when relevant
Description: When Court has to form opinion as to usages/tenets of body of men/family, constitution of religious/charitable foundation, or meaning of local/district words, opinions of persons having special means of knowledge are relevant.

Section_name: Opinion on relationship, when relevant
Description: When Court has to form opinion as to relationship, opinion expressed by conduct of person who as family member or otherwise has special means of knowledge is relevant: Provided not sufficient to prove marriage in Divorce Act or BNS Sec 82/84.

Section_name: Grounds of opinion, when relevant
Description: Whenever the opinion of any living person is relevant, the grounds on which such opinion is based are also relevant.

Section_name: In civil cases character to prove conduct imputed, irrelevant
Description: In civil cases the fact that the character of any person concerned is such as to render probable or improbable any conduct imputed to him, is irrelevant, except in so far as such character appears from facts otherwise relevant.

Section_name: In criminal cases previous good character relevant
Description: In criminal proceedings the fact that the person accused is of a good character, is relevant.

Section_name: Evidence of character or previous sexual experience not relevant in certain cases
Description: In prosecution for offences under BNS Sec 64-71, 74-78 or attempt, where consent is in issue, evidence of character of victim or previous sexual experience shall not be relevant on consent or quality of consent.

Section_name: Previous bad character not relevant, except in reply
Description: In criminal proceedings, the fact that the accused has a bad character, is irrelevant, unless evidence has been given that he has a good character, in which case it becomes relevant. Previous conviction is relevant as evidence of bad character.

Section_name: Character as affecting damages
Description: In civil cases, the fact that the character of any person is such as to affect the amount of damages which he ought to receive, is relevant.

Chapter_name: FACTS WHICH NEED NOT BE PROVED
Section_name: Fact judicially noticeable need not be proved
Description: No fact of which the Court will take judicial notice need be proved.

Chapter_name: FACTS WHICH NEED NOT BE PROVED
Section_name: Facts of which Court shall take judicial notice
Description: (1) The Court shall take judicial notice of: all laws in force in India; international treaties/agreements; proceedings of Constituent Assembly, Parliament, State Legislatures; seals of Courts/Tribunals/Notaries; accession, titles, signatures of public officers; existence, flag of recognised countries; divisions of time, geographical divisions, gazetted holidays; territory of India; commencement/termination of hostilities; officers of Court, advocates; rule of the road. (2) Court may resort to appropriate reference books/documents.

Chapter_name: FACTS WHICH NEED NOT BE PROVED
Section_name: Facts admitted need not be proved
Description: No fact needs to be proved in any proceeding which the parties thereto or their agents agree to admit at the hearing, or in writing before hearing, or by rule of pleading: Provided Court may in discretion require facts admitted to be proved otherwise.

Section_name: Proof of facts by oral evidence
Description: All facts, except the contents of documents may be proved by oral evidence.

Section_name: Oral evidence to be direct
Description: Oral evidence shall in all cases whatever be direct: if referring to fact seen, heard, perceived by sense, or opinion held, must be evidence of witness who saw, heard, perceived, or held opinion: Provided expert opinions in published treatises may be proved if author dead, un-found, or incapable.

Section_name: Proof of contents of documents
Description: The contents of documents may be proved either by primary or by secondary evidence.

Section_name: Primary Evidence
Description: Primary evidence means the document itself produced for inspection of Court. Explanations: Executed in parts = each part primary; executed in counterpart = primary against executing party; uniform process (printing/photos) = primary of rest; electronic/digital record created/stored in multiple files or proper custody = primary evidence; video recording simultaneously stored/broadcast = primary; multiple automated storage spaces/temp files = primary.

Section_name: Secondary evidence
Description: Secondary evidence includes: (i) certified copies; (ii) mechanical copies ensuring accuracy; (iii) copies made from or compared with original; (iv) counterparts against non-executing parties; (v) oral accounts of contents by person who saw it; (vi) oral admissions; (vii) written admissions; (viii) testimony of skilled examiner of voluminous documents.

Section_name: Proof of documents by primary evidence
Description: Documents shall be proved by primary evidence except in the cases hereinafter mentioned.

Section_name: Cases in which secondary evidence relating to documents may be given
Description: Secondary evidence may be given when: (a) original in possession of opponent/out of reach/bound to produce and fails after notice; (b) contents admitted in writing; (c) original destroyed/lost; (d) original not easily movable; (e) original is public document (Sec 74); (f) original permitted certified copy; (g) original consists of numerous accounts.

Section_name: Electronic or digital record
Description: Nothing in this Adhiniyam shall apply to deny the admissibility of an electronic or digital record in evidence on the ground that it is an electronic or digital record, and subject to Sec 63 shall have same legal effect, validity and enforceability as other document.

Section_name: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record
Description: The contents of electronic records may be proved in accordance with the provisions of Section 63.

Section_name: Admissibility of electronic records
Description: (1) Computer output (printed, stored, recorded, copied) deemed to be a document and admissible without further proof of original if conditions satisfied. (2) Conditions: produced during regular lawful control/use, information regularly fed in ordinary course, computer operating properly during material period, reproduces/derived from fed info. (3) Single computer includes networks/resources/intermediaries. (4) Certificate required identifying record, describing manner of production, verifying device parameters signed by person in charge and expert (as per Schedule).

Section_name: Rules as to notice to produce
Description: Secondary evidence under Sec 60(a) requires prior notice to produce as prescribed by law or reasonable under circumstances, except when document is notice itself, adverse party knows production required, obtained by fraud/force, original in Court, loss admitted, or person out of reach.

Section_name: Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document produced
Description: If a document is alleged to be signed or written wholly or in part by any person, the signature or handwriting of so much of document as is alleged must be proved to be in his handwriting.

Section_name: Proof as to electronic signature
Description: Except in case of secure electronic signature, if electronic signature of subscriber is alleged to be affixed, fact that it belongs to subscriber must be proved.

Section_name: Proof of execution of document required by law to be attested
Description: If required by law to be attested, shall not be used as evidence until one attesting witness called, if alive and subject to process: Provided not necessary for registered documents (other than wills) unless execution specifically denied.

Section_name: Proof where no attesting witness found
Description: If no attesting witness found, must be proved that attestation of at least one witness is in his handwriting, and signature of executing person is in handwriting of that person.

Section_name: Admission of execution by party to attested document
Description: The admission of a party to an attested document of its execution by himself shall be sufficient proof of its execution as against him, though it be a document required by law to be attested.

Section_name: Proof when attesting witness denies execution
Description: If the attesting witness denies or does not recollect the execution of the document, its execution may be proved by other evidence.

Section_name: Proof of document not required by law to be attested
Description: An attested document not required by law to be attested may be proved as if it was unattested.

Section_name: Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or proved
Description: (1) Signature, writing, or seal admitted/proved to satisfaction of Court may be compared with one to be proved. (2) Court may direct person present in Court to write words/figures for comparison. (3) Applies also to finger impressions.

Section_name: Proof as to verification of digital signature
Description: To ascertain whether digital signature is that of person, Court may direct production of Digital Signature Certificate or application of public key listed therein.

Section_name: Public and private documents
Description: (1) Public documents: acts/records of sovereign authority, official bodies/tribunals, public officers (legislative, judicial, executive) of India or foreign country; public records kept in State/UT of private documents. (2) All other documents are private.

Section_name: Certified copies of public documents
Description: Public officer having custody of public document shall give copy on demand + legal fees with certificate written at foot dated/subscribed with name, official title, seal ('certified copy').

Section_name: Proof of documents by production of certified copies
Description: Such certified copies may be produced in proof of the contents of the public documents or parts of the public documents of which they purport to be copies.

Section_name: Proof of other official documents
Description: Specifies mode of proof for: Central/State Acts, orders, notifications; Parliamentary/Legislative proceedings; Presidential/Gubernatorial proclamations; foreign executive/legislative acts; municipal body proceedings; foreign public documents.

Section_name: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies
Description: (1) Court shall presume genuine every document purporting to be certificate/certified copy declared by law admissible and certified by Central/State officer. (2) Shall presume officer held official character claimed.

Section_name: Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence, etc.
Description: Court shall presume genuine document produced as record/memorandum of evidence in judicial proceeding or confession by prisoner signed by Judge/Magistrate.

Section_name: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents
Description: Court shall presume genuineness of Official Gazette, newspaper, journal, or document directed by law to be kept, produced from proper custody.

Section_name: Presumption as to Gazettes in electronic or digital record
Description: Court shall presume genuineness of electronic/digital record purporting to be Official Gazette or record directed by law to be kept, produced from proper custody.

Section_name: Presumption as to maps or plans made by authority of Government
Description: Court shall presume maps/plans made by Central or State Government authority were so made and are accurate; but maps/plans for specific cause must be proved.

Section_name: Presumption as to collections of laws and reports of decisions
Description: Court shall presume genuineness of book printed/published under Government authority containing laws or court ruling reports.

Section_name: Presumption as to powers-of-attorney
Description: Court shall presume power-of-attorney executed before and authenticated by Notary Public, Court, Judge, Magistrate, Indian Consul/Vice-Consul was so executed/authenticated.

Section_name: Presumption as to electronic agreements
Description: Court shall presume electronic record purporting to be agreement containing electronic/digital signature of parties was concluded by affixing signature.

Section_name: Presumption as to electronic records and electronic signatures
Description: (1) In secure electronic record, Court presumes unaltered since specific point in time. (2) In secure electronic signature, Court presumes affixed with intention of signing/approving.

Section_name: Presumption as to Electronic Signature Certificates
Description: Court shall presume info listed in Electronic Signature Certificate is correct (except unverified subscriber info) if accepted by subscriber.

Section_name: Presumption as to certified copies of foreign judicial records
Description: Court may presume certified copy of foreign judicial record genuine/accurate if certified by Central Government representative.

Section_name: Presumption as to books, maps and charts
Description: Court may presume book, map, or chart referred to for public/general interest info was written/published by person, time, and place as stated.

Section_name: Presumption as to electronic messages
Description: Court may presume electronic message forwarded by originator through email server corresponds with message fed into computer, but no presumption as to sender.

Section_name: Presumption as to due execution, etc., of documents not produced
Description: Court shall presume document called for and not produced after notice was attested, stamped, and executed in manner required by law.

Section_name: Presumption as to documents thirty years old
Description: Where document 30 years old is produced from proper custody, Court may presume signature and handwriting is of person it purports to be, and duly executed/attested.

Section_name: Presumption as to electronic records five years old
Description: Where electronic record 5 years old is produced from proper custody, Court may presume electronic signature was affixed by person or authorised person.

Chapter_name: OF THE EXCLUSION OF ORAL EVIDENCE BY DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
Section_name: Evidence of terms of contracts, grants and other dispositions of property reduced to form of document
Description: When terms of contract, grant or property disposition reduced to document form, no evidence given in proof except document itself or admissible secondary evidence. Exceptions: public officer appointment in writing; wills admitted to probate.

Chapter_name: OF THE EXCLUSION OF ORAL EVIDENCE BY DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
Section_name: Exclusion of evidence of oral agreement
Description: When terms proved under Sec 94, no oral evidence admitted to contradict, vary, add to, or subtract from terms: Provisos allow proof of fraud/illegality, separate oral agreement on silent matters, condition precedent, subsequent modification, custom/usage.

Chapter_name: OF THE EXCLUSION OF ORAL EVIDENCE BY DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
Section_name: Exclusion of evidence to explain or amend ambiguous document
Description: When language used in document is on its face ambiguous or defective, evidence may not be given of facts which would show its meaning or supply defects.

Chapter_name: OF THE EXCLUSION OF ORAL EVIDENCE BY DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
Section_name: Exclusion of evidence against application of document to existing facts
Description: When language used in document is plain in itself, and applies accurately to existing facts, evidence may not be given to show that it was not meant to apply to such facts.

Chapter_name: OF THE EXCLUSION OF ORAL EVIDENCE BY DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
Section_name: Evidence as to document unmeaning in reference to existing facts
Description: When language used in a document is plain in itself, but is unmeaning in reference to existing facts, evidence may be given to show that it was used in a peculiar sense.

Chapter_name: OF THE EXCLUSION OF ORAL EVIDENCE BY DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
Section_name: Evidence as to application of language which can apply to one only of several persons
Description: When facts are such that language used might have been meant to apply to any one, and could not apply to more than one of several persons/things, evidence may be given showing which was intended.

Chapter_name: OF THE EXCLUSION OF ORAL EVIDENCE BY DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
Section_name: Evidence as to application of language to one of two sets of facts, to neither of which the whole correctly applies
Description: When language applies partly to one set of existing facts and partly to another, but whole does not apply correctly to either, evidence may be given showing which it was meant to apply to.

Chapter_name: OF THE EXCLUSION OF ORAL EVIDENCE BY DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
Section_name: Evidence as to meaning of illegible characters, etc.
Description: Evidence may be given to show meaning of illegible or not commonly intelligible characters, foreign, obsolete, technical, local, regional expressions, abbreviations, and words used in peculiar sense.

Chapter_name: OF THE EXCLUSION OF ORAL EVIDENCE BY DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
Section_name: Who may give evidence of agreement varying terms of document
Description: Persons who are not parties to a document, or their representatives in interest, may give evidence of any facts tending to show a contemporaneous agreement varying terms of document.

Chapter_name: OF THE EXCLUSION OF ORAL EVIDENCE BY DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE
Section_name: Saving of provisions of Indian Succession Act relating to wills
Description: Nothing in this Chapter shall be taken to affect any of the provisions of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 as to the construction of wills.

Section_name: Burden of proof
Description: Whoever desires any Court to give judgment as to any legal right or liability dependent on facts he asserts must prove that those facts exist. Burden of proof lies on that person.

Section_name: On whom burden of proof lies
Description: The burden of proof in a suit or proceeding lies on that person who would fail if no evidence at all were given on either side.

Section_name: Burden of proof as to particular fact
Description: The burden of proof as to any particular fact lies on that person who wishes the Court to believe in its existence, unless provided by law that proof lies on particular person.

Section_name: Burden of proving fact to be proved to make evidence admissible
Description: The burden of proving any fact necessary to be proved in order to enable any person to give evidence of any other fact is on person who wishes to give such evidence.

Section_name: Burden of proving that case of accused comes within exceptions
Description: When a person is accused of any offence, burden of proving existence of circumstances bringing case within General Exceptions or special exceptions in BNS or law is upon him, and Court presumes absence of such circumstances.

Section_name: Burden of proving fact especially within knowledge
Description: When any fact is especially within the knowledge of any person, the burden of proving that fact is upon him.

Section_name: Burden of proving death of person known to have been alive within thirty years
Description: When question is whether a man is alive or dead, and shown alive within 30 years, burden of proving dead is on person who affirms it.

Section_name: Burden of proving that person is alive who has not been heard of for seven years
Description: When question is whether a man is alive or dead, and proved not heard of for 7 years by those naturally hearing if alive, burden of proving alive shifts to person who affirms it.

Section_name: Burden of proof as to relationship in the cases of partners, landlord and tenant, principal and agent
Description: When shown acting as partners, landlord/tenant, or principal/agent, burden of proving they do not stand or ceased to stand in relationship is on person who affirms it.

Section_name: Burden of proof as to ownership
Description: When question is whether person is owner of anything shown in his possession, burden of proving he is not owner is on person who affirms he is not owner.

Section_name: Proof of good faith in transactions where one party is in relation of active confidence
Description: Where question is good faith of transaction between parties, one of whom stands in active confidence, burden of proving good faith is on party in active confidence.

Section_name: Presumption as to certain offences
Description: Where accused of offences in disturbed area or area of public disturbance over 1 month, and shown present where firearms/explosives used to attack armed forces, presumed to have committed offence.

Section_name: Birth during marriage, conclusive proof of legitimacy
Description: Fact that person born during continuance of valid marriage or within 280 days after dissolution (mother unmarried) is conclusive proof of legitimacy, unless no access shown.

Section_name: Presumption as to abetment of suicide by a married woman
Description: When suicide committed by married woman within 7 years of marriage and subjected to cruelty by husband/relatives, Court may presume abetment by husband/relatives.

Section_name: Presumption as to dowry death
Description: When question is dowry death under BNS Sec 80 and shown woman subjected to cruelty/harassment for dowry soon before death, Court shall presume person caused dowry death.

Section_name: Court may presume existence of certain facts
Description: Court may presume existence of facts likely happened in common course of natural events, human conduct, public/private business (e.g. stolen goods possession = thief; accomplice unworthy of credit unless corroborated; judicial/official acts regularly performed).

Section_name: Presumption as to absence of consent in certain prosecution for rape
Description: In prosecution for rape under BNS Sec 64(2), where sexual intercourse proved and woman states in evidence she did not consent, Court shall presume she did not consent.

Section_name: Estoppel
Description: When one person has, by declaration, act or omission, intentionally caused/permitted another to believe a thing true and act upon belief, neither he nor representative allowed in suit/proceeding to deny truth.

Section_name: Estoppel of tenant and of licensee of person in possession
Description: No tenant or licensee permitted during tenancy/licence to deny landlord/licensor had title at beginning of tenancy/licence.

Section_name: Estoppel of acceptor of bill of exchange, bailee or licensee
Description: No acceptor of bill of exchange permitted to deny drawer had authority to draw/endorse; no bailee/licensee permitted to deny bailor/licensor authority.

Section_name: Who may testify
Description: All persons competent to testify unless Court considers prevented from understanding questions or giving rational answers by tender years, extreme old age, body/mind disease.

Section_name: Witness unable to communicate verbally
Description: Witness unable to speak may give evidence by writing or signs in open Court (deemed oral evidence); Court shall take assistance of interpreter/special educator and videograph.

Section_name: Competency of husband and wife as witnesses in certain cases
Description: (1) In civil proceedings, parties and husband/wife are competent witnesses.(2) In criminal proceedings against any person, husband or wife is a competent witness.

Section_name: Judges and Magistrates
Description: No Judge/Magistrate compelled to answer questions as to conduct in Court except upon special order of superior Court, but may be examined on other matters in presence.

Section_name: Communications during marriage
Description: No married/formerly married person compelled or permitted to disclose communication made during marriage without consent, except in suits between married persons or crimes against each other.

Section_name: Evidence as to affairs of State
Description: No one permitted to give evidence derived from unpublished official records relating to affairs of State except with permission of officer at head of department.

Section_name: Official Communications
Description: No public officer compelled to disclose communications made to him in official confidence when public interest would suffer by disclosure.

Section_name: Information as to commission of offences
Description: No Magistrate, police officer, or revenue officer compelled to say when/where he got information as to commission of offences or offences against public revenue.

Section_name: Professional communications
Description: (1) No advocate permitted to disclose client communications, document contents/conditions, or advice given without express consent. Exceptions: illegal purpose communications; crime/fraud observed since commencement. (2) Applies to interpreters, clerks, and employees of advocates.

Section_name: Privilege not waived by volunteering evidence
Description: Party giving evidence at own instance not deemed to consent to Sec 132 disclosure; calling advocate as witness consents only if questioning on privileged matters.

Section_name: Confidential communication with legal advisers
Description: No one compelled to disclose confidential communications with legal adviser unless offering self as witness to explain evidence given.

Section_name: Production of title-deeds of witness not a party
Description: Witness not a party not compelled to produce title-deeds, pledgee/mortgagee documents, or criminating documents unless agreeing in writing.

Section_name: Production of documents or electronic records which another person, having possession, could refuse to produce
Description: No one compelled to produce documents in possession or electronic records under control which another person would be entitled to refuse, unless last-mentioned person consents.

Section_name: Witness not excused from answering on ground that answer will criminate
Description: Witness not excused from answering relevant questions on ground that answer will criminate or expose to penalty/forfeiture: Proviso protects answer from arrest/prosecution except false evidence.

Section_name: Accomplice
Description: An accomplice shall be a competent witness against an accused person; and a conviction is not illegal if it proceeds upon the corroborated testimony of an accomplice.

Section_name: Number of witnesses
Description: No particular number of witnesses shall in any case be required for the proof of any fact.

Section_name: Order of production and examination of witnesses
Description: Order of production and examination of witnesses regulated by civil/criminal procedure law and practice, and in absence by Court discretion.

Section_name: Judge to decide as to admissibility of evidence
Description: (1) Judge asks party in what manner alleged fact is relevant and admits if relevant. (2) Fact admissible only on proof of another fact must be proved first unless undertaking given. (3) Relevancy dependent on first fact proved.

Section_name: Examination of witnesses
Description: (1) Examination by party calling = examination-in-chief. (2) Examination by adverse party = cross-examination. (3) Examination subsequent to cross-examination by party calling = re-examination.

Section_name: Order of examinations
Description: (1) Chief -> Cross -> Re-examination. (2) Chief and cross relate to relevant facts; cross not confined to chief. (3) Re-examination directed to explanation of cross; new matter allows further cross.

Section_name: Cross-examination of person called to produce a document
Description: Person summoned to produce document does not become witness by mere production and cannot be cross-examined unless called as witness.

Section_name: Witnesses to character
Description: Witnesses to character may be cross-examined and re-examined.

Section_name: Leading questions
Description: (1) Any question suggesting answer expected is leading question. (2) Must not be asked in chief or re-examination if objected to, except with Court permission. (3) Permitted for introductory, undisputed, or proved matters. (4) May be asked in cross-examination.

Section_name: Evidence as to matters in writing
Description: Witness may be asked if contract/grant was in document; if yes or about contents, adverse party may object until document produced or secondary evidence allowed.

Section_name: Cross-examination as to previous statements in writing
Description: Witness may be cross-examined as to previous written statements without showing writing; but to contradict, attention must be called to parts before proving.

Section_name: Questions lawful in Cross-examination
Description: Questions lawful to: (a) test veracity; (b) discover identity/position; (c) shake credit by injuring character (proviso restricts general immoral character/sexual experience questions in rape cases).

Section_name: When witness to be compelled to answer
Description: If question relates to matter relevant to suit/proceeding, provisions of Section 137 shall apply.

Section_name: Court to decide when question shall be asked and when witness compelled to answer
Description: Court decides whether witness compelled to answer irrelevant questions affecting credit; proper if truth affects credibility, improper if remote or disproportionate.

Section_name: Question not to be asked without reasonable grounds
Description: No question under Sec 151 ought to be asked unless person asking has reasonable grounds for thinking imputation well-founded.

Section_name: Procedure of Court in case of question being asked without reasonable grounds
Description: If Court opinion question asked without reasonable grounds by advocate, may report to High Court or governing authority.

Section_name: Indecent and scandalous questions
Description: Court may forbid indecent or scandalous questions unless relating to facts in issue or necessary to determine facts in issue.

Section_name: Questions intended to insult or annoy
Description: Court shall forbid any question intended to insult or annoy, or needlessly offensive in form.

Section_name: Exclusion of evidence to contradict answers to questions testing veracity
Description: No evidence given to contradict answer to question shaking credit/character (prosecuted for false evidence if false); Exceptions: previous conviction, impeaching impartiality.

Section_name: Question by party to his own witness
Description: (1) Court in discretion may permit party calling witness to put questions allowable in cross-examination (hostile witness). (2) Does not disentitle party from relying on evidence.

Section_name: Impeaching credit of witness
Description: Credit impeached by: (a) testimony of persons believing witness unworthy of credit; (b) proof of bribe/corrupt inducement; (c) proof of former inconsistent statements.

Section_name: Questions tending to corroborate evidence of relevant fact, admissible
Description: Witness corroborating relevant fact may be questioned on circumstances observed at/near time or place to corroborate testimony.

Section_name: Former statements of witness may be proved to corroborate later testimony as to same fact
Description: Former statement made at/about time fact took place or before investigating authority may be proved to corroborate testimony.

Section_name: What matters may be proved in connection with proved statement relevant under Section 26 or Section 27
Description: When statement under Sec 26 or 27 proved, all matters may be proved to contradict, corroborate, or impeach/confirm credit.

Section_name: Refreshing memory
Description: (1) Witness under examination may refresh memory by referring to writing made by self or read at time of transaction. (2) May refer to copy with Court permission; expert may refer to professional treatises.

Section_name: Testimony to facts stated in document mentioned in Section 162
Description: Witness may testify to facts in document mentioned in Sec 162 without specific recollection if sure facts were correctly recorded.

Section_name: Right of adverse party as to writing used to refresh memory
Description: Writing used to refresh memory produced and shown to adverse party, who may cross-examine witness upon it.

Section_name: Production of documents
Description: (1) Witness summoned shall bring document to Court despite objections. (2) Court decides validity of objection. (3) Cabinet/Ministerial communications with President protected from production.

Section_name: Giving, as evidence, of document called for and produced on notice
Description: Party calling for document on notice and inspecting it is bound to give it as evidence if producing party requires.

Section_name: Using, as evidence, of document production of which was refused on notice
Description: Party refusing to produce document on notice cannot afterwards use it as evidence without consent of other party or Court order.

Section_name: Judge's power to put questions or order production
Description: Judge may ask any question in any form at any time to discover proof of relevant facts, or order production; parties cannot object or cross-examine without leave.

Chapter_name: OF IMPROPER ADMISSION AND REJECTION OF EVIDENCE
Section_name: No new trial for improper admission or rejection of evidence
Description: Improper admission or rejection of evidence shall not be ground of itself for new trial or reversal if sufficient evidence exists independently to justify decision.

Section_name: Repeal and savings
Description: (1) The Indian Evidence Act, 1872 is hereby repealed. (2) Pending applications, trials, inquiries, investigations, proceedings or appeals shall be dealt with under Indian Evidence Act, 1872 as if this Adhiniyam had not come into force.
